```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                      warning = TRUE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
```

## From an analysis to an auditable bundle

An analytical result and its written presentation serve different purposes.
`mira_info_long()` computes results; `mira_report_freq_long()` preserves those
results, writes a table archive and Quarto source, and optionally renders a
document. Reporting an existing result does not refit it. The intended readers
are analysts preparing a reproducible deliverable and researchers checking
where a reported number came from. Complete the
[getting-started tutorial](frequentist-long-getting-started.html) first.

Consider a separate synthetic retinal clinic cohort of 48 adults with diabetic
macular edema (DME). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is recorded as ETDRS
letter scores at baseline, month 3 and month 6; larger scores indicate better
measured acuity. Each participant contributes one eligible study eye, selected
by a prespecified random choice at enrolment if both eyes are eligible, before
any follow-up result is available. Only that eye is represented in this table.
The `study_eye` column records laterality; `subject_id` identifies the independent
participant and their single study-eye series. The examples do not model two
eyes within a participant.

We assume the same acuity protocol and best correction at repeated visits.
The [DRCR Retina Network's measurement protocol](https://public.jaeb.org/drcrnet/stdy/149)
illustrates why acuity assessment needs a defined procedure. The generator
below is not a reconstruction of that study, an eligibility rule, or an estimate
of a real treatment effect. It includes participant heterogeneity, visit noise,
and rounded letter scores. No values are clipped to force a favorable result.

```{r report-data}
library(MIRA)
set.seed(4830)
n <- 48L
retina <- data.frame(
  subject_id = sprintf("O%03d", seq_len(n)),
  study_eye = sample(c("Right", "Left"), n, replace = TRUE)
)
baseline_acuity <- rnorm(n, 58, 7)
retina$bcva_t0 <- round(baseline_acuity + rnorm(n, 0, 2))
retina$bcva_t1 <- round(baseline_acuity + 3 + rnorm(n, 0, 3))
retina$bcva_t2 <- round(baseline_acuity + 6 + rnorm(n, 0, 4))
acuity_columns <- c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(retina$subject_id),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(retina[acuity_columns]))),
  all(as.matrix(retina[acuity_columns]) >= 0),
  all(as.matrix(retina[acuity_columns]) <= 100))
analysis <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "subject_id", covariates = character(0),
  time_vars = acuity_columns,
  time_labels = c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6"),
  improvement_direction = "higher", stable_threshold = 5,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(inherits(analysis, "mira_info_long"))
```

The bounds check describes the generated chart-score example, not universal
test limits for every acuity protocol. `stable_threshold = 5` is an illustrative
five-letter classification band, not a validated MCID or a treatment-response
definition. A gain of more than five letters receives the configured observed-change
classification `Improved` in `clinical_direction`; that classification does not assess measurement error
or establish an individual causal treatment benefit.

First identify the result to be preserved. Select month 6 minus baseline by
its named visit columns, then independently reconstruct its paired mean.

```{r reported-endpoint}
endpoint <- analysis$change[analysis$change$from == "bcva_t0" &
  analysis$change$to == "bcva_t2", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(endpoint) == 1L, endpoint$n == nrow(retina),
  isTRUE(all.equal(endpoint$mean_change, mean(retina$bcva_t2 - retina$bcva_t0))))
knitr::kable(endpoint[c("from_label", "to_label", "n", "mean_change", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")],
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("From", "To", "Pairs", "Mean gain", "Lower", "Upper"),
  caption = "The BCVA result to archive: month-6-minus-baseline ETDRS letters, with a pointwise 95% mean-change interval.")
```

The observed mean gain is `r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$mean_change)` letters,
with interval `r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$ci_lower)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$ci_upper)` letters among `r endpoint$n` paired study
eyes from the same number of participants. This is uncertainty about a mean
change, not the range of individual gains. Without a comparison strategy it
does not identify a treatment effect. Reporting must preserve this result
rather than manufacture a stronger clinical conclusion.

The core result includes descriptive summaries and paired changes even with
`analyses = "none"`. A report cannot create an analysis that was disabled in
the original call. For inference, review the paired samples and the assumptions
described in the [descriptive](frequentist-long-descriptive-analysis.html) and
[advanced-model](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html) tutorials.

## Start with the result already understood

You now have an analytical object called `analysis`. The new question is how
to keep its exact tables and the instructions for presenting them. No new
data, estimand or analysis method is needed. Reuse this object rather than
repeating the analysis inside the reporting call.

```{r first-source-bundle}
first_bundle <- mira_report_freq_long(
  x = analysis,
  output_dir = tempfile("mira-first-report-"),
  format = "html",
  render = FALSE,
  open = FALSE
)
data.frame(
  source_exists = file.exists(first_bundle$source),
  payload_exists = file.exists(first_bundle$payload),
  html_rendered = unname(first_bundle$rendered[["html"]])
)
stopifnot(identical(first_bundle$mira_result, analysis))
```

The two source checks are true and `html_rendered` is false. That is the
intended outcome: a **source-only bundle** stores the result, table archive
and report instructions without producing a finished HTML document. The
descriptor's `source` and `payload` fields locate those files. It is safe to
inspect and preserve this bundle without Quarto or TeX.

Use a newly allocated directory for each independent bundle. This avoids
collisions during repeated vignette builds and keeps generated artifacts out
of the package source and installation directories. Set `format` explicitly:
the function's default requests **both HTML and PDF**. Also set `render` and
`open` explicitly in scripts: their defaults are `TRUE` and `interactive()`.

## Add study metadata and choose visible sections

Keep the same `analysis` and source-only mode. The next bundle changes only
presentation: a meaningful title, authors, fixed document date, filename and
selected sections help a colleague identify the study. A second directory
keeps this independent presentation separate from `first_bundle`.

```{r source-bundle}
bundle <- mira_report_freq_long(
  x = analysis,
  output_dir = tempfile("mira-retina-bcva-"),
  output_file = "Retinal BCVA longitudinal analysis",
  format = "html",
  title = "Study-eye BCVA trajectories in diabetic macular edema",
  subtitle = "Synthetic one-study-eye cohort: BCVA in ETDRS letters",
  author = c("A. Researcher", "B. Statistician"),
  date = as.Date("2026-10-01"),
  sections = c("methods", "data_quality", "overview", "descriptives",
               "missingness", "change", "diagnostics", "conclusions"),
  render = FALSE, open = FALSE, quiet = TRUE
)
stopifnot(inherits(bundle, "mira_report_freq_long"))
stopifnot(identical(basename(bundle$source),
                    "retinal_bcva_longitudinal_analysis.qmd"))
basename(bundle$source)
bundle$rendered
bundle$render_errors
```

`render = FALSE` still writes the QMD source, runtime R script, compressed RDS
payload, eligible CSV tables and manifest. It does not call Quarto. Consequently
`rendered` is false, `render_errors` is `NA` rather than a failure message, and
`files` is empty. `expected_files` describes targets; it does not certify
that documents exist or were successfully generated in this invocation.

The stem is normalized to lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscores.
Supply a stem without an extension: `"report.html"` becomes `"report_html"`.
The default output directory is relative to the working directory, so explicit
directory management is preferable in reproducible scripts.

## Inspect sources, preserved objects and exported numbers

The descriptor is an invisible return value that is also printed automatically.
Save it to obtain actual artifact paths instead of predicting filenames.

```{r inspect-bundle}
sources <- c(bundle$source, bundle$runtime, bundle$payload,
             bundle$results_manifest)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(sources)), length(bundle$files) == 0L,
          !any(bundle$rendered), all(is.na(bundle$render_errors)))
data.frame(artifact = basename(sources), bytes = file.info(sources)$size)
payload <- readRDS(bundle$payload)
names(payload)
stopifnot(identical(bundle$mira_result, analysis),
          identical(payload$result$descriptives, analysis$descriptives),
          identical(payload$result$change, analysis$change),
          identical(payload$result$settings, analysis$settings),
          identical(attr(payload$result$descriptives, "mira_metric_names"),
                    attr(analysis$descriptives, "mira_metric_names")),
          identical(names(payload), c("result", "extra_objects", "report")))
```

Keep the QMD, runtime and payload together when moving the bundle. The runtime
contains report helpers; it does not replace the external R packages needed
to print native model objects or draw stored plots. The payload always contains
the original result, including details omitted from the document. It may contain
participant identifiers and source observations: review the whole bundle before
sharing it, using the same data-governance rules as for the analysis itself.

The manifest maps each table to its owning object path, outcome and relative
CSV filename. Do not use a hard-coded filename when a manifest lookup suffices.

```{r manifest}
manifest <- utils::read.csv(bundle$results_manifest, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(names(manifest),
  c("outcome", "path", "file", "original_class", "rows", "columns")))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path(bundle$output_dir, manifest$file))),
          length(bundle$result_files) == nrow(manifest))
manifest_excerpt <- head(manifest[, c("outcome", "path", "rows", "columns")], 8)
manifest_excerpt$path <- paste0("`", manifest_excerpt$path, "`")
knitr::kable(manifest_excerpt,
             caption = "An excerpt of the machine-readable table manifest.")
desc_row <- manifest[manifest$path == "outcome$descriptives", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(desc_row) == 1L)
archived <- utils::read.csv(file.path(bundle$output_dir, desc_row$file),
                            check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(archived) == nrow(analysis$descriptives),
          identical(archived$time, analysis$descriptives$time),
          identical(archived$n, analysis$descriptives$n),
          isTRUE(all.equal(archived$mean, analysis$descriptives$mean,
                           tolerance = 1e-12)))
```

CSV p-values retain their numeric values; display rounding does not turn them
into strings such as `"<0.001"`. CSV is a tabular interchange format, however:
list-valued cells become text and matrix-valued columns may expand. Use the
RDS payload for exact R objects and their attributes, including metric-name
maps. RDS files should be read only from trusted sources.

The checks compare the report input before serialization and the relevant
tables, settings and metric-name attributes after reading it back. For fitted
models, compare fixed parameters and their covariance matrices, as in the
[complete workflow](frequentist-long-complete-workflow.html), rather than
requiring `identical()` for a whole model containing environments or pointers.

## Analyse and report in one call

Supplying `data` forwards `...` to `mira_info_long()`. This creates a fresh
analysis; it is convenient for a fully specified script. Passing the saved
`analysis` instead preserves the already reviewed analytical object. Arguments
in `...` are rejected when an existing result is supplied. Do not supply both
`x` and `data`; a data frame passed as `x` is also accepted as direct data.

```{r direct-report}
direct <- mira_report_freq_long(
  data = retina, id = "subject_id", outcomes = "bcva",
  covariates = character(0),
  time_vars = c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2"),
  time_labels = c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6"),
  improvement_direction = "higher", stable_threshold = 5,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE,
  output_dir = tempfile("mira-direct-"), output_file = "direct_analysis",
  format = "html", render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
stopifnot(inherits(direct$mira_result, "mira_info_long"),
          file.exists(direct$payload))
names(direct$mira_result$descriptives)
```

Incompatible inputs fail before bundle creation. These checks deliberately
exercise two API errors; an unrelated error would fail the assertions.

```{r incompatible-inputs}
both_inputs <- tryCatch({
  mira_report_freq_long(x = analysis, data = retina, render = FALSE,
                        output_dir = tempfile("mira-invalid-"), open = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
unused_analysis_args <- tryCatch({
  mira_report_freq_long(x = analysis, analyses = "none", render = FALSE,
                        output_dir = tempfile("mira-invalid-"), open = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(grepl("not both", both_inputs, fixed = TRUE),
          grepl("only when data is supplied", unused_analysis_args, fixed = TRUE))
```

Here explicit `outcomes = "bcva"` declares the name and prefixes metrics
with `bcva_`. Selecting `time_vars` alone in the earlier call left the outcome
inferred and its metrics generic. The report follows the stored conventions.
The [multiple-outcome tutorial](frequentist-long-multiple-outcomes.html)
demonstrates safe extraction through the `mira_metric_names` attribute.

## Choose content and presentation settings

Sections appear in scientific order when eligible results exist. Selecting a
section does not enable a missing analysis, and the order of the `sections`
vector does not reorder the report.

| Section keys | Content |
|:--|:--|
| `abstract`, `methods`, `data_quality`, `overview` | Available outcomes, resolved settings, detected variables and sample structure |
| `descriptives`, `missingness`, `change`, `arms` | Visit summaries, availability, paired changes and enabled arm analyses |
| `correlations`, `variability`, `trajectories` | Cross-visit associations, ICC/variation and participant-level changes |
| `models`, `robustness` | Fitted and advanced analyses; robust inference, effect sizes, multiplicity and sensitivity |
| `outliers`, `figures`, `diagnostics` | Diagnostic flags, stored plots and relevant recorded warnings/failures |
| `conclusions` | Difference between first and last observed means; a descriptive summary |
| `appendix` | Eligible `extra_objects` |
| `frequencies` | A component of that name if present; standard results need not contain it |
| `all` | Every eligible route above |

The generated `conclusions` section subtracts observed means. With incomplete
follow-up those means may refer to different participants; the difference is
neither necessarily a paired mean change nor a treatment effect.

```{r focused-report}
auxiliary <- stats::lm(bcva_t2 ~ bcva_t0, data = retina)
focused <- mira_report_freq_long(
  analysis, output_dir = tempfile("mira-focused-"), format = "html",
  sections = c("descriptives", "change", "appendix"),
  include_complete_output = FALSE,
  extra_objects = list(baseline_followup_association = auxiliary),
  max_table_rows = 6, max_table_columns = 8, digits = 4, max_depth = 50,
  render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
focused_manifest <- utils::read.csv(focused$results_manifest,
                                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(manifest, focused_manifest),
  identical(readRDS(focused$payload)$result$descriptives,
            analysis$descriptives),
  identical(readRDS(focused$payload)$result$settings, analysis$settings),
  inherits(readRDS(focused$payload)$extra_objects[[
    "baseline_followup_association"]], "lm"))
archived_auxiliary <- readRDS(focused$payload)$extra_objects[[
  "baseline_followup_association"]]
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(stats::coef(archived_auxiliary), stats::coef(auxiliary))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(stats::vcov(archived_auxiliary), stats::vcov(auxiliary))),
  !any(grepl("extra_objects", focused_manifest$path, fixed = TRUE))
)
```

`max_table_rows` (default `Inf`) limits displayed rows, with a truncation note. Wide tables
are split into blocks by `max_table_columns` (default 12), repeating comparison keys when
space permits. PDF blocks have at most eight columns and DOCX blocks at most
seven. `digits` (default 3) controls display precision (1--10), including a lower display
threshold for recognized p-values. These choices and `sections` leave the
eligible-table CSV archive unchanged, as the assertion above verifies.

`max_depth` is different: it limits traversal for both visible results and
CSV export. Lowering it can omit deeply nested tables, although the payload
remains complete. Retain the default of 50 unless there is a specific reason
to restrict traversal. Numeric depth/column/precision values are converted to
integers by the implementation; use whole numbers to make the intent explicit.

The following intentionally shallow archive illustrates that distinction.
The full-depth manifest remains the appropriate starting point for an audit.

```{r archive-depth}
shallow <- mira_report_freq_long(
  analysis, output_dir = tempfile("mira-shallow-"), format = "html",
  max_depth = 1, render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
shallow_manifest <- utils::read.csv(shallow$results_manifest,
                                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(shallow_manifest) < nrow(manifest),
          all(shallow_manifest$path %in% manifest$path),
          identical(readRDS(shallow$payload)$result$change, analysis$change))
data.frame(full_depth_tables = nrow(manifest),
           shallow_tables = nrow(shallow_manifest))
```

`include_complete_output` is retained for API compatibility and recorded in
the configuration. It currently does not change the visible report: eligible
results are already traversed without a duplicate complete-output appendix.
It never removes the full result from the payload. `extra_objects` are
preserved there and appear only with `appendix` or `all`; they are **not**
exported to CSV. The auxiliary BCVA regression describes a baseline/follow-up association in
letters, not an adjusted treatment effect. It is retained separately from the
paired mean-change result already interpreted.

## Add OCT anatomy without replacing the BCVA result

A multi-outcome object uses the same reporting interface. Outcome tables are
placed in outcome-specific subdirectories; shared context has an empty outcome
key. Opposite favorable directions require explicit scientific configuration.

The next named copy retains the same people, study eyes and BCVA observations.
It adds an anatomical outcome: OCT mean retinal thickness in the central
1-mm-diameter subfield, in micrometres. We use `cmt` as the local column prefix
for this specified measurement (often called central subfield thickness, CST).
Assume one OCT platform and segmentation convention across visits. Device-
specific thicknesses or a center-point measurement are not silently pooled.

This generator shares a modest baseline association with BCVA but adds separate
anatomical noise and reductions; the resulting numbers are illustrative.
Decreasing thickness describes less thickening in this edema example, not
necessarily a visual improvement or a validated surrogate endpoint. The
[DRCR structure-function study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17123615/)
explains why OCT anatomy cannot reliably substitute for visual acuity.

```{r multi-report}
set.seed(4831)
retina_multi <- retina
anatomy <- 420 - 2 * (retina$bcva_t0 - mean(retina$bcva_t0)) + rnorm(n, 0, 35)
retina_multi$cmt_t0 <- round(anatomy + rnorm(n, 0, 12))
retina_multi$cmt_t1 <- round(anatomy - 30 + rnorm(n, 0, 20))
retina_multi$cmt_t2 <- round(anatomy - 65 + rnorm(n, 0, 25))
stopifnot(identical(retina_multi[c("subject_id", "study_eye", acuity_columns)], retina),
  all(as.matrix(retina_multi[c("cmt_t0", "cmt_t1", "cmt_t2")]) > 0))
multi <- mira_info_long(
  retina_multi, id = "subject_id", outcomes = c("bcva", "cmt"),
  improvement_direction = c(bcva = "higher", cmt = "lower"),
  stable_threshold = c(bcva = 5, cmt = 25),
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
multi_bundle <- mira_report_freq_long(
  multi, output_dir = tempfile("mira-retinal-multi-report-"),
  format = "all", render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
multi_manifest <- utils::read.csv(multi_bundle$results_manifest,
                                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
table(multi_manifest$outcome)
stopifnot(all(c("bcva", "cmt") %in% multi_manifest$outcome),
          identical(names(multi_bundle$rendered), c("html", "pdf", "docx")))
```

The five-letter and 25-micrometre bands are teaching settings in different
units. They do not establish clinical response criteria, and their numerical
changes must not be pooled. This multi-outcome report archives separate
analyses, not a joint model of visual function and retinal anatomy. IOP as a
safety measure with unknown favorable direction is demonstrated in the
[multiple-outcome article](frequentist-long-multiple-outcomes.html).

`mira_detect_long` objects from `inspect_only = TRUE` are accepted too. They
produce context and diagnostics, with no outcome analyses to invent.

```{r detection-report}
detection <- mira_info_long(retina, id = "subject_id", outcomes = "bcva",
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", inspect_only = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
detection_bundle <- mira_report_freq_long(
  detection, output_dir = tempfile("mira-detection-report-"),
  format = "html", sections = c("methods", "data_quality", "diagnostics"),
  render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
stopifnot(file.exists(detection_bundle$source))
```

## Safe regeneration

The default `overwrite = FALSE` protects existing source artifacts, selected
render targets, the manifest and planned CSV paths before writing them. This
deliberate error is captured and checked so that it remains a visible example
of the contract rather than aborting the tutorial.

```{r overwrite-contract}
collision <- tryCatch({
  mira_report_freq_long(analysis, output_dir = bundle$output_dir,
    output_file = "Retinal BCVA longitudinal analysis", format = "html",
    render = FALSE, open = FALSE)
  NULL
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(is.character(collision), grepl("already exist", collision))
cat(collision, "\n")
regenerated <- mira_report_freq_long(
  analysis, output_dir = bundle$output_dir,
  output_file = "Retinal BCVA longitudinal analysis", format = "html",
  sections = c("overview", "descriptives"),
  render = FALSE, open = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE
)
stopifnot(file.exists(regenerated$source))
```

Use one directory per independent report even when stems differ: all bundles
use `results_manifest.csv` and `results/`. Overwriting removes obsolete CSVs
listed in a prior valid manifest only when safely contained under `results/`.
It does not clean unrelated files. Bundle writes span several files and are
not transactional; inspect a partial bundle after a filesystem error.

## Rendering HTML, PDF and DOCX

Rendering requires the `knitr` and `quarto` R packages **and** the Quarto CLI.
PDF also needs a compatible TeX installation. DOCX generation does not require
Microsoft Word. `format = "all"` expands to HTML, PDF and DOCX; a character
vector can request a subset. Source preparation remains useful without any
external renderer. Installation instructions are in the package README and
the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).

The following executable branch is deliberately opt-in so package builds do
not require external tools. To verify it with tools already available, set
`MIRA_RENDER_VIGNETTE_FORMATS=html,docx,pdf` before building this vignette, and
inspect the returned status and documents. Request a subset if TeX is absent.
It prepares a new source-only bundle and renders it externally, one format at
a time. The [Quarto PDF options](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/pdf.html)
allow `latex-auto-install: false` to prevent automatic TeX package installation.
Here it is written into a **copy** of the QMD before any render attempt; the
preserved analytical result is unchanged. The standard Quarto PDF wrapper is
retained so its normal repeated compilation can resolve references.

```{r optional-rendering}
requested <- Sys.getenv("MIRA_RENDER_VIGNETTE_FORMATS", "")
render_status <- data.frame(
  format = c("html", "pdf", "docx"),
  status = "not requested", error = NA_character_
)
if (nzchar(requested)) {
  requested <- trimws(strsplit(requested, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
  stopifnot(all(requested %in% c("html", "pdf", "docx")))
  deferred_bundle <- mira_report_freq_long(
    analysis, output_dir = tempfile("mira-rendered-"), format = requested,
    sections = c("methods", "descriptives", "change", "diagnostics"),
    render = FALSE, open = FALSE, quiet = FALSE
  )
  safe_source <- file.path(deferred_bundle$output_dir, "deferred-no-install.qmd")
  qmd <- readLines(deferred_bundle$source, warn = FALSE)
  if ("pdf" %in% requested) {
    pdf_line <- which(qmd == "  pdf:")
    stopifnot(length(pdf_line) == 1L)
    qmd <- append(qmd, "    latex-auto-install: false", after = pdf_line)
  }
  writeLines(qmd, safe_source)
  for (fmt in requested) {
    target <- file.path(deferred_bundle$output_dir, paste0("deferred-no-install.", fmt))
    problem <- tryCatch({
      quarto::quarto_render(safe_source, output_format = fmt,
        output_file = basename(target), execute_dir = deferred_bundle$output_dir,
        quiet = FALSE, as_job = FALSE)
      if (!file.exists(target) || file.info(target)$size <= 0) {
        stop("External renderer returned without a nonempty document.")
      }
      NA_character_
    }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
    selected <- match(fmt, render_status$format)
    render_status$status[selected] <- if (is.na(problem)) "rendered externally" else "render failed"
    render_status$error[selected] <- problem
  }
  stopifnot(!any(deferred_bundle$rendered), length(deferred_bundle$files) == 0L)
} else {
  cat("External rendering not requested; source bundles were verified.\n")
}
knitr::kable(render_status, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "External document rendering: one explicit status per format.")
```

A `render failed` row is a recorded failure, not a successful document. Inspect
its message and resolve the stated dependency or environment problem before
relying on that format. The ledger describes this external operation; the
source-only MIRA descriptor remains unchanged, as the assertion verifies.
This branch checks that a nonempty document was created; publication still
requires visual and scientific inspection of that document. In the direct
`mira_report_freq_long(..., render = TRUE)` workflow, missing R rendering
packages instead stop the call after sources are written, with no descriptor.

For a deferred render, keep the companion files together and call
`quarto::quarto_render(regenerated$source, output_format = "html",
execute_dir = regenerated$output_dir)`. This external operation writes the
document but does not retroactively update the earlier MIRA descriptor; use
a new `mira_report_freq_long(..., render = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)` invocation
when a fresh descriptor is needed.

Each requested format is attempted independently once rendering starts.
Inspect `rendered`, `render_errors` and `files` for the current invocation.
Per-format failures produce an aggregate warning and retain source artifacts;
missing R rendering packages instead cause an error after the sources are
written. A previous rendered document may remain after an overwrite attempt
fails or skips rendering. Its presence is not proof of current success.
`quiet` controls Quarto console output, not validation warnings or the printed
descriptor. `open = TRUE` opens the first successful document and should be
avoided in automated work.

## Reproducibility and scientific review

Record the seed, analysis configuration, software versions and rendering
environment together with the bundle. Its timestamp is operational metadata,
so regenerated files need not be byte-identical. Exact preserved analytical
objects and manifest-linked tables provide stronger traceability than copied
numbers. A generated report does not assess study design, choose an estimand,
justify missing-data assumptions or establish scientific validity.

```{r reporting-session}
packageVersion("MIRA")
sessionInfo()
```

to connect study design, diagnostics, inference and the final bundle.
